docs.title: VAG memory usage in Sheaf: analysis and design notes
Context
docs.text: GPT-2 124M through value-and-grad consumes ~13 GB of RAM. Reference point: JAX on the same model uses ~2-5 GB. The gap is ~3x, not marginal. This document records what was tried in April 2026 to close the gap, why it failed, and what a correct implementation would require.

docs.title: Approach: replace static unrolling with stablehlo.while
docs.text:
The hypothesis was that the memory cost came from IREE holding all N × body copies in memory simultaneously due to static unrolling. The plan:

  1. Emit stablehlo.while for the forward reduce (one body copy, runtime loop)
  2. Emit a second stablehlo.while for the backward VJP that recomputes forward activations then applies the gradient
  3. Store per-iteration carries in a pre-allocated buffer [N+1, ...]

docs.title: Infrastructure built
docs.text:
• stablehlo.while emission with condition and body regions (sheaf/src/lowering/stablehlo/while_ops.rs)
  • Region capture in the emitter (begin_region / end_region)
  • Dynamic slice/update with runtime indices (emit_dynamic_slice_axis0, emit_dynamic_update_slice_axis0)
  • ElemKind::DeepStacked: recursive flattening of nested VecTuple collections to leaf tensors, with a template for reconstruction
  • stack_vec_tuple: descends to leaf tensors, stacks each leaf on axis 0
  • build_virtual_tuple_from_leaves: reconstructs the nested virtual tuple matching an elem_template
  • Free-variable threading through the while state (body references to outer SSA values must be explicit state components in StableHLO while regions)
  • Let-bound alias handling (block-p = bp) with layout propagation
  • use_while_loops flag on CodeGenerator + dispatch in builtins.rs

docs.title: Result
docs.text:
Runtime memory: ~15 GB on a simple case, ~60 GB on the full benchmark before the process was killed. Worse than the 13 GB baseline.

Total code added: ~1500 lines in the codegen, ~8 bugs successively fixed (VecTuple handling, deep nesting, aliases, layouts, free vars, deep-stack recursion, etc.). The commit was reverted on b499ff1.

docs.title: Diagnosis error
docs.text:
The 13 GB baseline was assumed to come from MLIR code size (12 unrolled copies of a transformer block in the SSA graph). In reality, it comes from activations that must be kept live for the backward pass: Q, K, V, attention scores, layer norm intermediates, etc. A transformer block generates ~500 MB of activations per layer; 12 layers × 500 MB = ~6 GB of activations alone, independent of how the MLIR is structured.

Replacing static unrolling with stablehlo.while reduces MLIR size but does nothing about activation storage. IREE still needs to allocate buffers for all live intermediate tensors.

docs.title: Worse: state pass-through amplifies the cost
docs.text: In our implementation, the collection (stacked transformer block parameters) was passed through the while state as pass-through tensors. IREE appears to materialize these tensors inside the while loop iteration rather than aliasing them. For GPT-2 this is ~2 GB × 12 iterations worth of materialization overhead, hence the 60 GB explosion.

docs.title: Recomputation in the backward doubled the code
docs.text: The backward while body contained both the re-materialized forward pass and the backward pass. For GPT-2, that is ~300 MLIR ops per iteration, and IREE's optimizer appears not to handle this structure well -- possibly unrolling the while internally since N=12 is known, defeating the purpose.

docs.title: What JAX does
docs.text: Study of jax/_src/lax/control_flow/loops.py (_scan_transpose_fancy around line 935) and jax/_src/ad_checkpoint.py.

docs.title: JAX scan VJP architecture
docs.text:
1. Scan is a first-class primitive with its own transpose rule. The backward is itself a scan with reverse=True.

  2. Residuals are identified by partial evaluation. JAX traces the forward body, applies pe.partial_eval_jaxpr_*, and determines exactly which intermediate values are needed for the backward. Typically: inputs to non-linear primitives (matmul operands, exp/log inputs, softmax outputs). NOT all activations.

  3. Forward scan outputs the residuals as extensive outputs (stacked on axis 0, one entry per iteration). The forward scan signature becomes (carry, eres_1, eres_2, ...) where each eres_i is [N, ...res_shape_i].

  4. Backward scan consumes the residuals. It iterates in reverse, and at each step uses the residual stored at that iteration to compute the local VJP. The backward scan signature includes the residuals as inputs.

  5. The scan primitive maps to XLA/StableHLO while but XLA has scan-specific optimizations (buffer donation, aliasing, memory planning) that do not kick in on a generic while we emit by hand.

docs.title: jax.checkpoint / remat is separate
docs.text: Rematerialization (recomputing forward instead of storing) is a separate decorator (@jax.checkpoint) that a user applies explicitly. The default behavior is to store residuals, not recompute. Our attempt to build rematerialization into the default path was a mistake.

docs.title: Minimum viable path
docs.text:
1. Partial evaluation of the reduce body to classify each intermediate as "residual needed for backward" vs "dead after forward". This is the hardest piece.

  2. Extend the forward reduce to produce residuals as stacked outputs. The current generate_reduce_scan produces only the final carry. It needs to also produce [N, ...] tensors for each residual.

  3. Rewrite generate_scan_vjp to be a backward scan that consumes residuals at each step via dynamic_slice. The body is the local VJP using the sliced residual, not a re-materialized forward.

  4. Actually use stablehlo.while only when IREE's compiler handles it well. For transformer-like bodies with N=12, it may be better to keep static unrolling and focus on reducing activation count per layer.

docs.title: Key decisions to make
docs.text:
• Is partial evaluation done on CompiledExpr pre-codegen, or on emitted MLIR? JAX does it on jaxprs (pre-emission). Sheaf has no equivalent pass.
  • Who owns the residual identification policy? JAX exposes jax.checkpoint_policies for the user. Sheaf should probably default to "save matmul inputs" initially.
  • How to represent residuals in CompiledExpr IR? They are extra outputs of a scan, so the scan primitive's output type changes.

docs.title: What NOT to repeat
docs.text:
• Do not add stablehlo.while without first understanding what gets stored. MLIR size was never the bottleneck.
  • Do not pass large unchanging tensors through the while state as pass-throughs. IREE materializes them. Find a way to reference them as hoisted-out values.
  • Do not build rematerialization into the default path. It is a separate opt-in mechanism and should stay that way.
  • Do not attempt a rewrite of the codegen for scan without first writing a targeted microbenchmark (small model, not GPT-2) that measures exactly what gets allocated. We flew blind for most of this session.
